subject.title: Next Sprint B: model-input validation guardrails

question: Should configured model `input` values treat `audio` and `video` as valid metadata to preserve, invalid deployment-blocking values, or metadata that is valid only behind explicit runtime capability gates?
rationale: Current main already preserves audio/video in the public config path while another registry path rejects them and media-understanding trusts user-declared image capability, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Preserve Metadata, Gate Runtime Use
options.body: Keep audio/video as valid catalog metadata, but add capability-aware runtime selection/diagnostics and clear docs for which paths can actually consume each modality.

options.title: Reject Unsupported Inputs
options.body: Tighten configured model validation to fail deployment for unsupported modalities, with migration or doctor guidance for existing configs and generated catalogs.

options.title: Clamp Catalog Inputs
options.body: Normalize unsupported modalities out of generated/configured catalog rows before registry use, trading metadata fidelity for a simpler text/image runtime contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve Metadata, Gate Runtime Use
recommendation.body: Keep audio/video as valid catalog metadata, but add capability-aware runtime selection/diagnostics and clear docs for which paths can actually consume each modality.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the strongest current routing candidate from blame and issue timeline evidence across the schema/type/registry surfaces.
